'''Alexander Wai Ping-kong''' ({{lang-zh|衞炳江}}) is a former Deputy President and Provost of the [[Hong Kong Polytechnic University]], who served from 1 March 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polyu.edu.hk/publications/excel/issue/201909/highlight/prof-alexander-wai-appointed-as-new-deputy-president-and-provost|title=Prof. Alexander Wai appointed as new Deputy President and Provost|website=Hong Kong Polytechnic University|date=September 2019}}</ref> He had served the Hong Kong Polytechnic University for over 20 years since 1996.<ref name="scmp_20200722"/> He assumed the position of President and Vice-Chancellor of the [[Hong Kong Baptist University]] on 1 February 2021.<ref name="scmp_20200722">{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/education/article/3094299/local-scholar-alexander-wai-gets-top-job-hong-kongs|title=Local scholar Alexander Wai gets top job at Hong Kong’s Baptist University after beating 200 candidates in global search|first1=Ho-him|last1=Chan|first2=Kang-chung|last2=Ng|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|date=22 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bunews.hkbu.edu.hk/news/people/hkbu-appoints-professor-alexander-wai-ping-kong-as-new-president-and-vice-chancellor|title=HKBU appoints Professor Alexander Wai Ping-kong as new President and Vice-Chancellor|website=Hong Kong Baptist University|date=22 July 2020}}</ref>

In late July 2021, at his first press conference since taking up his position at Baptist University and slightly over a year after the enactment of the [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong National Security Law]],  Wai said that the university had no plans to limit research on areas such as [[Hong Kong independence movement|Hong Kong independence]] and [[human rights abuses in Xinjiang]]; management would not advocate their colleagues breaking the law, however. At the same time, Baptist University together with at least two other public universities in Hong Kong introduced mandatory undergraduate education on national security in the form of seminars and talks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/education/article/3142592/hong-kong-baptist-university-makes-national-security|title=At least 3 Hong Kong universities make national security education compulsory for students|first=Ho-him|last=Chan|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|date=26 July 2021|access-date=27 July 2021}}</ref>

==Campus visit during the November 2019 siege==
In November 2019, during the [[Siege of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University]] which marked an escalation of the [[2019–2020 Hong Kong protests]], Wai, who was vice-president of the university at the time, visited the campus together with council chairman [[Lam Tai-fai]] and fellow vice-president Ben Young. As they were reaching the communal building, they were stopped by a student who complained about the management figures having failed in their duties by not helping the students. When Wai was told to help clean the kitchen whose cleanliness he had criticized in response, he agreed and cleaned the kitchen for around 30 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hongkongfp.com/2019/11/22/hong-kong-polyu-management-briefly-clean-squalid-canteen-blockaded-campus|title=Hong Kong PolyU management briefly clean squalid canteen at blockaded campus|first=Kris|last=Cheng|work=[[Hong Kong Free Press]]|date=22 November 2019|access-date=28 July 2021}}</ref>
